decision_time: reassessment checkpoint — after new ordered investigation result information becomes available

guideline.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign 2026
guideline.citation: Prescott HC, et al. Crit Care Med 2026;54:725-812

design_notes: Agent 3 provides initial treatment recommendations at processed reassessment checkpoints.
Agent 3 uses a sequential accumulation graph rather than a mutually exclusive branching graph.
Treatment decisions are evaluated in the order antimicrobial timing, fluids, vasopressors, and MAP target.
Each node has a closed answer set.
The model may use only patient information available by the current checkpoint cutoff.
Guideline scopes are frozen offline and injected verbatim at runtime.
Treatment recommendations accumulate into one final treatment plan.
The main Agent 3 safety risk is over-treatment, particularly unnecessary fluid or vasopressor treatment in patients with non-septic mimics or limited tolerance of resuscitation.
The four antimicrobial timing labels in TX1 are provisional because Figure 7 specifies a four-value closed set but does not explicitly list all four labels.

TX1.title: Antimicrobial timing
TX1.question: Based on the current checkpoint patient state and supplied guideline evidence, what is the appropriate antimicrobial timing strategy?
TX1.scope_source: SSC 2026 antimicrobial timing block; stmt_019 retained as contextual support for infectious-versus-noninfectious reassessment

stmt_016: possible, probable, or definite septic shock
stmt_017: probable or definite sepsis without shock
stmt_018: if concern persists, antimicrobials within 3 hours
stmt_019: supports rapid assessment of infectious versus noninfectious causes
stmt_020: low likelihood of infection without shock

rules: Use only information available by the current checkpoint cutoff.
For possible, probable, or definite septic shock, use the within_1h pathway.
For probable or definite sepsis without shock, use the within_1h pathway.
For possible sepsis without shock, use the within_3h pathway only after a time-limited rapid investigation if concern for infection persists.
For low likelihood of infection without shock, defer antimicrobials while monitoring closely.
Do not infer infection solely from one biomarker or test result.
Do not use stmt_021 for this ED treatment node because it addresses prehospital antimicrobial administration when transport to in-hospital evaluation is expected to exceed 60 minutes.
The antimicrobial timing answer labels are provisional and should be confirmed with the team.

TX2.title: Initial fluid resuscitation
TX2.question: Based on the current checkpoint patient state and supplied guideline evidence, should IV crystalloid fluid resuscitation be given now?

stmt_010: at least 30 mL/kg IV crystalloid in first 3 hours
stmt_044: balanced crystalloids preferred over 0.9% saline during initial resuscitation
stmt_045: crystalloids alone preferred over crystalloids plus supplemental albumin
stmt_049: dynamic measures preferred to guide fluid resuscitation

rules: Use only information available by the current checkpoint cutoff.
The decision is whether initial IV crystalloid resuscitation should be given now.
Sepsis-induced hypoperfusion, septic shock, or sepsis-induced hypotension support fluid resuscitation.
Use crystalloids as first-line fluid.
Balanced crystalloids are preferred over 0.9% saline during initial resuscitation.
Do not recommend starches or gelatin.
Use dynamic measures when available to help guide additional fluid resuscitation.
Do not automatically give fluids solely because sepsis is suspected.
Consider evidence that argues against additional fluid administration, including an already adequate fluid state or concern for fluid intolerance.
stmt_048 is intentionally excluded because it addresses fluid strategy after 30 mL/kg has already been given with persistent hypoperfusion.

TX3.title: Initial vasopressor treatment
TX3.question: Based on the current checkpoint patient state and supplied guideline evidence, should vasopressor therapy be started now?

stmt_011: vasopressor support if hypotension persists following initial crystalloid resuscitation
stmt_012: peripheral vasopressor initiation preferred over delaying for central access
stmt_053: norepinephrine first-line over dopamine, epinephrine, or selepressin
stmt_055: norepinephrine first-line over vasopressin or angiotensin II

rules: Use only information available by the current checkpoint cutoff.
Start vasopressor therapy when hypotension persists despite appropriate initial fluid resuscitation or when the clinical state otherwise meets the supplied guideline criteria.
Do not start vasopressors solely because sepsis is suspected.
If vasopressor therapy is indicated, norepinephrine is the first-line agent.
Do not delay necessary vasopressor initiation solely to obtain central venous access.
This node does not decide vasopressor escalation after initial norepinephrine.
Statements concerning vasopressin addition, epinephrine escalation, inotropes, dobutamine, or levosimendan are intentionally excluded from this initial start/hold decision.

TX4.title: Initial MAP target
TX4.question: If vasopressor-supported septic shock is present, what initial MAP target should be used?

stmt_014: septic shock age 65 years or older

rules: Use only information available by the current checkpoint cutoff.
Return not_applicable when septic shock requiring a vasopressor MAP target is not present.
For adults with septic shock younger than 65 years, use target_65.
For adults with septic shock age 65 years or older, use target_60_65.
Do not invent higher MAP targets outside the closed set.

TREATMENT_COMPLETE.description: All four Agent 3 initial-treatment decisions have been evaluated and accumulated into the final treatment plan.

ABSTAIN.description: Agent 3 failed to produce a valid grounded response after the permitted repair attempt.

node_output_schema.answer: one value from the current node allowed_answers

supporting_evidence.patient_finding: patient-specific information available at the current checkpoint
supporting_evidence.statement_id: statement id from the current node scope
supporting_evidence.quote: verbatim quote from the injected guideline statement
supporting_evidence.implication: brief explanation connecting the patient finding and guideline to the selected answer

opposing_evidence.patient_finding: patient-specific information arguing against the selected answer
opposing_evidence.statement_id: statement id from current scope or null
opposing_evidence.quote: verbatim quote when statement_id is provided, otherwise null
opposing_evidence.implication: brief explanation of why this argues against the selected treatment

missing_information: clinically relevant information unavailable at the current checkpoint

V1.name: closed_answer_validation
V1.description: The answer returned for each node must belong to that node's allowed_answers.

V2.name: citation_scope_validation
V2.description: Every cited guideline statement id must belong to the current node's frozen scope.

V3.name: verbatim_quote_validation
V3.description: Every quoted guideline passage must appear verbatim in the guideline text injected for the current node.

accumulation.completion_condition: TX1, TX2, TX3, and TX4 have each produced a valid response.
